segments.name: Coding agents
segments.description: Agents that read, edit, test and ship code, from terminal/IDE assistants to cloud agents that open pull requests.

segments.name: General, computer-use and browser agents
segments.description: Agents that operate a browser or computer, or complete open-ended multi-step tasks for a consumer or knowledge worker.

segments.name: Enterprise and workflow agents
segments.description: Platforms for building and governing agents over company data and business systems (CRM, M365, Google Workspace, enterprise search).

segments.name: Customer-support agents
segments.description: Vertical agents that resolve customer conversations across chat, email and voice, usually priced per outcome or conversation.

segments.name: Agent frameworks and platforms for builders
segments.description: SDKs, frameworks and managed infrastructure that developers use to build and run their own agents.

segments.name: Research agents
segments.description: Agents that plan and run long web/enterprise research and return cited reports.

features.name: Autonomous multi-step execution
features.description: Plans and carries out multi-step tasks with tool calls without a human driving each step.

features.name: Background / cloud async runs
features.description: Tasks continue running remotely (cloud sandbox or hosted runtime) while the user is away.

features.name: Scheduling and event triggers
features.description: Runs on a cron/schedule or in response to events (webhooks, PRs, tickets).

features.name: Computer / browser use
features.description: Can drive a GUI or web browser (clicks, typing, screenshots) rather than only APIs.

features.name: Code execution and file editing
features.description: Can edit files and execute code or shell commands in a sandbox or local environment.

features.name: MCP / tool integrations
features.description: Supports Model Context Protocol servers or comparable tool/connector extension points.

features.name: Persistent memory / project context
features.description: Retains instructions or learnings across sessions (memory files, long-term memory stores).

features.name: Multi-agent orchestration / subagents
features.description: Coordinates several agents (subagents, handoffs, parallel tasks) on one job.

features.name: Human-in-the-loop approvals
features.description: Asks a person to approve or edit consequential actions or plans.

features.name: SSO and enterprise admin controls
features.description: Admin governance such as SSO/SCIM, RBAC, audit logs, usage limits, data controls.

features.name: Open source / self-hostable
features.description: Core code under an open-source license and/or self-hostable by the customer.

features.name: API / SDK access
features.description: Programmatic access (API, SDK, CLI headless mode) to run the agent from other software.

features.name: Observability, testing and evals
features.description: Tracing, monitoring, simulations or evaluation tooling for agent behaviour.

features.name: Web research with citations
features.description: Searches the web or enterprise data and returns sourced answers or reports.

features.name: Multi-model / bring-your-own model
features.description: Lets the user choose among several models or providers.

features.name: No-code / low-code agent builder
features.description: Business users can define agents or workflows in natural language or visual tools.

features.name: Enterprise data and app connectors
features.description: Prebuilt connectors to business systems (CRM, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, ticketing).

features.name: Public self-serve pricing
features.description: Vendor publishes plan prices (not only 'contact sales').

products.name: Claude Code
products.summary: Agentic coding tool for terminal, IDE, desktop and web with subagents, hooks, MCP, scheduled cloud tasks and an Agent SDK; runs on Anthropic or Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry.
products.pricingModel: Included in paid Claude plans: Pro $20/mo ($17 annual), Max from $100/mo, Team Standard $25/seat/mo ($20 annual) and Premium $125/seat/mo ($100 annual), Enterprise $20/seat/mo annual (20-seat minimum) plus usage at API rates; or pay-per-token via API/cloud providers (pricing page, fetched 2026-10-20).

products.name: OpenAI Codex
products.summary: OpenAI's coding agent family: open-source Codex CLI, IDE extension, desktop app and cloud-based Codex web, signed in with a ChatGPT plan or API key.
products.pricingModel: Bundled with ChatGPT plans (Plus $20/mo and above, Business, Enterprise/Edu) with shared rolling usage allowances; API-key per-token usage also possible. Exact plan tiers and limits differ between secondary sources (low confidence).

products.name: GitHub Copilot (cloud agent and agent mode)
products.summary: Copilot cloud/coding agent takes assigned issues, works in an ephemeral firewalled environment and opens draft PRs; agent mode and Copilot CLI are also included in plans.
products.pricingModel: Usage-based GitHub AI Credits (1 credit = $0.01): Free; Pro $10/mo; Pro+ $39/mo; Max $100/mo; Business and Enterprise per-seat with pooled credits. Completions do not consume credits. (github.com/features/copilot/plans, fetched.)

products.name: Cursor
products.summary: AI code editor and CLI with local agent, cloud agents, Automations (scheduled/event-triggered background agents), Bugbot PR review, mobile app and enterprise controls.
products.pricingModel: Per-seat/usage-based subscriptions. Cursor's own pages describe a restructured lineup ('The X Subscription') alongside legacy Hobby/Pro $20/Pro+ $60/Ultra $200 and Teams seats; figures conflict across sources, so treat prices as low confidence and check cursor.com/pricing.

products.name: Devin (incl. Devin Desktop, formerly Windsurf)
products.summary: Autonomous cloud software-engineering agent with MCP marketplace, API, schedules/Automations and enterprise (including dedicated single-tenant VPC) deployment; Windsurf editor now sold as Devin Desktop.
products.pricingModel: Per Devin docs/pricing page (via search snippets): Free, Pro $20/mo, Max $200/mo, Teams $80/mo minimum plus $40/full seat, Enterprise negotiated; usage billed in ACUs/credits. Older Windsurf pricing posts show different numbers (medium confidence).

products.name: Gemini CLI / Antigravity CLI
products.summary: Gemini CLI is Google's Apache-2.0 terminal agent (MCP, GEMINI.md); since 2026-06-18 consumer tiers moved to the Antigravity CLI while Gemini CLI remains for enterprise licences and paid API keys.
products.pricingModel: Gemini CLI: API-key usage billed, enterprise via Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise or Google Cloud. Consumer access now via Antigravity CLI under Google AI plans; plan prices and free-tier terms conflict across third-party sources (low confidence).

products.name: Replit Agent
products.summary: Browser-based agent that builds, tests (in a real browser) and deploys apps from chat; supports remote MCP servers, background tasks, parallel work and enterprise SSO/SCIM.
products.pricingModel: Credit/effort-based within plans. Replit's blog gives Core $20/mo and Pro $100/mo; Agent modes are Free/Power/Max (+Auto). Third-party pages quote different Core/Pro figures (medium confidence).

products.name: ChatGPT Work (successor to ChatGPT agent / Operator)
products.summary: OpenAI's goal-driven agent that returns finished files and can work for hours; reportedly replaced ChatGPT agent mode (which absorbed Operator in July 2025), with a cloud browser for browser workflows.
products.pricingModel: No separate subscription; draws on each ChatGPT plan's usage allowance (secondary sources). Legacy ChatGPT agent had message caps (Plus 40/mo, Pro 400/mo).

products.name: Claude computer use (API tool)
products.summary: API toolset (GA on Claude API and Google Cloud, beta on AWS/Bedrock/Foundry) that lets Claude see screenshots and drive a mouse/keyboard in a sandbox the developer provides.
products.pricingModel: Pay-per-token API usage; each screenshot costs roughly 1,000-1,800 input tokens. No separate fee found. Rates not read from the pricing page.

products.name: Manus
products.summary: General-purpose cloud agent with Wide Research (up to 20 parallel subtasks), browser operator and desktop app; Meta said it would keep the subscription service running.
products.pricingModel: Credit-based: free daily credits; Pro from about $20/mo with from 4,000 monthly credits (annual discount); Team from $20/seat/mo (help-centre and docs pages).

products.name: Perplexity Comet
products.summary: Agentic AI browser with an assistant that acts across tabs, fills forms and runs background tasks; free to download since Oct 2025, with enterprise permission controls.
products.pricingModel: Browser free for everyone (since 2025-10-02); paid Perplexity plans (Pro/Max) add agent capacity; Enterprise tiers. Agent limits per tier differ across secondary sources (low confidence).

products.name: Microsoft Copilot Studio
products.summary: Low-code platform to build agents with tools, MCP, computer use, event-triggered autonomous runs and multi-agent orchestration, governed through Power Platform.
products.pricingModel: Copilot Credits: pay-as-you-go about $0.01/credit billed via Azure; capacity pack $200/mo for 25,000 credits; pre-purchase commit units (Microsoft pricing/Learn pages via search snippets).

products.name: Salesforce Agentforce
products.summary: Salesforce's agent platform (Atlas Reasoning Engine) with native MCP client, Agentforce Voice, Agentforce Observability (formerly Command Center) and Slack/CRM integration.
products.pricingModel: Consumption: Flex Credits $500 per 100,000 credits, 20 credits (about $0.10) per standard action, 30 for voice; Agentforce user licence $5/user/mo (requires credits); per-conversation/resolution model also listed.

products.name: Gemini Enterprise (formerly Agentspace)
products.summary: Google's work-agent platform with no-code Workflow Builder (formerly Agent Designer), Agent Gallery, Deep Research and Microsoft 365/Workspace connectors.
products.pricingModel: Per-seat editions (Business, Standard, Plus, Frontline); launch pricing reported at $21 (Business) and $30 (Standard/Plus) per seat/mo, but current prices are quote-based and custom ADK agents bill separately (secondary sources; low confidence).

products.name: Glean (Work AI platform and Agents)
products.summary: Permission-aware enterprise search and agent platform with no-code agents, hosted MCP server and gateway, and agents that run with the triggering user's permissions.
products.pricingModel: Not published. Third-party estimates (about $40-50+/user/mo, large annual minimums) are unverified (low confidence).

products.name: Sierra
products.summary: Enterprise customer-experience agent platform (Agent OS, no-code Agent Studio, Agent SDK) across chat, voice, email and messaging.
products.pricingModel: Outcome-based pricing (pay when the agent completes the task); rates are negotiated and not public. Reported valuation and ARR figures come from secondary sources (low confidence).

products.name: Decagon
products.summary: Support-agent platform built on natural-language Agent Operating Procedures (AOPs), with voice (ElevenLabs), simulations and Watchtower monitoring.
products.pricingModel: Not published; per-conversation default with a per-resolution option. Rates, contract sizes and valuation come from third-party sources and conflict (low confidence).

products.name: Intercom Fin
products.summary: Customer agent that resolves conversations in Intercom or other helpdesks (Zendesk, Salesforce), with Procedures, Simulations and Fin Voice.
products.pricingModel: $0.99 per outcome (resolution or configured procedure handoff); sources disagree on whether a monthly minimum applies; helpdesk seats extra when used inside Intercom.

products.name: LangGraph (and LangSmith Deployment)
products.summary: MIT-licensed low-level framework for long-running stateful agents with durable execution, human-in-the-loop and memory; deployable via LangSmith Deployment (cloud, hybrid, self-hosted).
products.pricingModel: Library free (MIT). LangSmith: Developer free (1 seat), Plus $39/seat/mo plus usage, Enterprise custom (pricing page via search snippet).

products.name: OpenAI Agents SDK
products.summary: MIT-licensed Python SDK with handoffs, guardrails, tracing, sessions, MCP tools and realtime/voice agents; works with 100+ other LLMs.
products.pricingModel: SDK free; pay for model/API usage.

products.name: Claude Agent SDK
products.summary: Python and TypeScript library exposing Claude Code's agent loop, tools, hooks, subagents, MCP, permissions and sessions; MIT-licensed repo but governed by Anthropic Commercial Terms.
products.pricingModel: SDK free; API-key billing for model usage (third parties may not offer claude.ai login or rate limits).

products.name: Microsoft Agent Framework
products.summary: MIT-licensed .NET/Python framework (successor to AutoGen and Semantic Kernel) with graph workflows, checkpointing, human-in-the-loop and OpenTelemetry; reported 1.0 GA in April 2026.
products.pricingModel: Framework free; hosted agents on Azure Foundry billed separately (not verified).

products.name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
products.summary: Managed, framework- and model-agnostic agent infrastructure: Runtime, Gateway (APIs to MCP tools), Identity, Memory, Browser, Code Interpreter, Observability, Evaluation, Policy.
products.pricingModel: Consumption-based with no minimums; GA Oct 2025; Runtime example rates $0.0895/vCPU-hour and $0.00945/GB-hour (v1); short-term memory moved to usage-based pricing in Oct 2026 (AWS pages via search snippets).

products.name: ChatGPT deep research
products.summary: ChatGPT mode that drafts an editable research plan, browses and returns a cited report; now also offered inside ChatGPT Work with a separate allowance.
products.pricingModel: Included in ChatGPT plans with tiered allowances (Limited on Free/Go, Expanded on Plus, Maximum on Pro); exact current counts not found (older figures were 25/month Plus, 250 Pro).

products.name: Gemini Deep Research (app and API agent)
products.summary: Autonomous research agent in the Gemini API via the Interactions API (standard and Max versions, April 2026 previews) with collaborative planning, MCP and File Search; also surfaced in Gemini Enterprise.
products.pricingModel: API usage on paid tiers during public preview; consumer limits by Google AI plan conflict across sources (low confidence).

strengths: Every major vendor now offers cloud/background agents plus MCP, e.g. Claude Code, Cursor Automations, Copilot cloud agent and Devin.
Distribution is bundled into existing subscriptions (Claude plans, ChatGPT plans, GitHub Copilot).
weaknesses: Pricing is volatile and hard to compare: Copilot moved to AI credits, Cursor restructured plans, Devin retired Core.
Consumer free tiers are being withdrawn (Gemini CLI free access ended 2026-06-18).
opportunities: Scheduled and event-triggered agents (Cursor Automations, Claude cloud scheduled tasks, Devin Automations) expand use from interactive coding to CI-style operations.
Enterprise-grade deployment (dedicated VPC, Bedrock/Vertex routing, managed settings) opens regulated buyers.
threats: Platform vendors bundle agents (GitHub delegating to Claude and Codex) and may commoditize standalone tools.
Usage-based billing makes heavy agent use unpredictable for buyers, pressuring margins and loyalty.

strengths: Capable browser/computer agents exist as products (Perplexity Comet, Manus) and as APIs (Claude computer use GA).
weaknesses: Products churn quickly: OpenAI's ChatGPT agent was reportedly replaced by ChatGPT Work.
Computer-use agents depend on screenshots (about 1,000-1,800 tokens each) and need sandboxing.
opportunities: Free distribution (Comet free since Oct 2025) and Meta's Manus acquisition could bring agents to mass-market channels.
threats: Prompt injection is a stated, ongoing risk requiring isolation and human confirmation.
Platform vendors can absorb standalone agent features into their assistants.

strengths: Vendors own the business data and identity layer: Salesforce CRM, Microsoft Power Platform/M365, Google Workspace, Glean's permission-aware index.
MCP is spreading across platforms (Agentforce native client, Copilot Studio, Glean MCP server).
weaknesses: Consumption pricing is complex (Flex Credits, Copilot Credits, quote-based seats), and Glean and Gemini Enterprise do not publish current prices.
opportunities: Governance features such as observability, credit limits and admin-controlled MCP can differentiate in security-sensitive firms.
Agent marketplaces (AgentExchange, Agent Gallery) create ecosystem lock-in.
threats: Suite lock-in disadvantages cross-ecosystem buyers, and builder platforms like AgentCore can bypass suites.
Agents running with user or maker credentials create access-control and cost-control risks.

strengths: Outcome-based pricing aligns spend with results: Intercom Fin at $0.99 per outcome, Sierra pay-per-outcome.
All three offer voice plus text channels and testing tooling.
weaknesses: Rates for Sierra and Decagon are not public and outcome definitions can be opaque.
opportunities: Voice and procedure/AOP authoring extend automation beyond FAQ deflection to transactions.
threats: Helpdesk and CRM incumbents bundle agents (Agentforce, Zendesk AI agents) with competing price points.
Per-resolution billing rises as agents improve, inviting buyer pushback.

strengths: Strong open-source base: LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK and Microsoft Agent Framework are all MIT-licensed.
Managed infrastructure (AgentCore) is framework- and model-agnostic.
weaknesses: Fragmentation: AutoGen and Semantic Kernel moved to maintenance mode in favour of Microsoft Agent Framework, forcing migrations.
opportunities: Observability, evaluation and policy layers (OpenTelemetry, AgentCore Evaluation/Policy, LangSmith) are monetizable add-ons.
threats: Model vendors ship opinionated SDKs (Claude Agent SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK) that may pull builders into their ecosystems.
Cloud-native runtimes may commoditize independent frameworks.

strengths: Deep research is shipped by the largest model vendors with citations and editable plans.
weaknesses: Usage limits and plan names change often and are poorly documented, and exact quotas were not verifiable.
opportunities: API access (Gemini Interactions API with MCP and File Search) lets research agents be embedded in products.
threats: Research features are being folded into broader agents (deep research inside ChatGPT Work, Gemini Enterprise), reducing standalone differentiation.

strengths: Broad surfaces (terminal, IDE, desktop, web) with subagents, hooks, MCP and scheduled cloud tasks.
Deployable via Teams/Enterprise or Bedrock, Vertex and Foundry with managed settings.
weaknesses: Included in paid plans only (Free excludes Claude Code), and subscription limits can push heavy users to API-rate billing.
Claude models only.
opportunities: Agent SDK and Slack/GitHub integrations extend it into automation and team workflows.
threats: Bundled competitors (Copilot, Codex via ChatGPT) and Cursor compete on price and distribution.
Subscription rate limits remain a pressure point for power users.

strengths: Open-source CLI (Apache-2.0) plus IDE, desktop and cloud surfaces under one ChatGPT sign-in.
Documented approval modes and enterprise managed configuration.
weaknesses: Usage allowances are shared and change often; sources disagree on tiers and limits.
opportunities: GitHub-integrated code review and large ChatGPT user base for cross-sell.
threats: Competes with Claude Code and Cursor on agent quality, and with GitHub Copilot on distribution.

strengths: Native to GitHub issues and PRs, with firewalled ephemeral environments and approval gating for workflows.
Multi-model support and delegation to third-party agents on Pro+/Max.
weaknesses: Shift to usage-billed AI credits adds cost uncertainty; free tier excludes the cloud agent.
opportunities: Huge installed base and pooled organization credits for Business/Enterprise.
threats: Reliance on partners' models while those partners ship competing agents (Claude Code, Codex).

strengths: Cloud agents and Automations (cron plus GitHub/Slack/Linear events) with MCP and memory.
Enterprise SSO/SCIM, MCP allowlists and Protected Git Scopes.
weaknesses: Pricing restructured with conflicting public figures (Plus/Premium/Super vs legacy Pro/Pro+/Ultra).
opportunities: Mobile app and Bugbot expand beyond the editor into review and operations.
threats: Depends on third-party frontier models whose vendors sell their own agents.

strengths: Mature autonomous cloud agent with MCP marketplace, API, schedules/Automations and single-tenant VPC deployment.
weaknesses: Pricing history is complicated (ACUs, retired Core plan, Windsurf-to-Devin Desktop rebrand).
opportunities: Windsurf/Devin Desktop adds an IDE surface alongside cloud agents.
threats: Foundation-model and platform vendors ship competing cloud coding agents.

strengths: Goal-to-deliverable agent inside the largest consumer assistant; always asks before consequential actions.
weaknesses: Predecessor ChatGPT agent was retired quickly; users report Work cannot drive a logged-in browser session (secondary sources).
opportunities: Connected apps and bundled plan allowance can attract knowledge workers.
threats: Browser-native competitors (Perplexity Comet) and Manus under Meta.

strengths: Low-code builder with multi-agent orchestration, computer use, MCP and event triggers; admin-level credit limits.
weaknesses: Credit metering varies by action type and can reach more than 100 credits per response.
opportunities: Microsoft 365 footprint and Power Platform governance.
threats: Salesforce and Google suites compete for the same buyers.

strengths: Atlas reasoning engine on top of CRM data; native MCP client; Observability with tracing and Datadog/Splunk hooks; voice.
weaknesses: Flex Credits per-action pricing is intricate; Flex Credits and per-conversation pricing cannot mix in one org (secondary source).
opportunities: AgentExchange and Slack can extend agent reach inside Salesforce customers.
threats: Support-specialist vendors (Sierra, Decagon, Fin) sell per outcome and may undercut.

strengths: Outcome-based model, voice and chat, no-code Agent Studio plus developer SDK.
weaknesses: Rates not public; billable-resolution definitions unclear to buyers (secondary reports).
opportunities: Voice benchmark leadership and developer SDK for complex flows.
threats: Salesforce Agentforce, Decagon and Intercom Fin compete at lower or published prices.

strengths: Transparent $0.99 per outcome pricing that works on other helpdesks; Procedures, Simulations and voice.
weaknesses: Cost scales with success and sources disagree on minimums.
opportunities: Helpdesk-agnostic offer can win accounts on Zendesk and Salesforce.
threats: Incumbent helpdesks and Sierra/Decagon undercutting or out-featuring.

strengths: MIT-licensed, durable execution and human-in-the-loop; deployment options from cloud to self-hosted.
weaknesses: Low-level framework with no no-code builder; more engineering required.
opportunities: LangSmith observability and Deployment monetize production usage.
threats: Vendor SDKs and cloud runtimes (OpenAI Agents SDK, AgentCore, Microsoft Agent Framework) compete.

strengths: Framework- and model-agnostic managed stack: Runtime, Gateway, Identity, Memory, Browser, Code Interpreter, Observability, Evaluation, Policy.
weaknesses: AWS-only service; consumption pricing needs careful estimation and pricing pages are in flux.
opportunities: Lets enterprises run open-source frameworks (LangGraph, CrewAI, Strands) on managed infrastructure.
threats: Competes with Azure Foundry hosted agents and Google's agent platform.
